notes.block: Devanagari, U+0900-U+097F. Words are runs of these letters and signs. The avagraha ऽ (U+093D) is a letter here: Bhojpuri writes it inside and at the end of words (कऽ, हऽ).
notes.notWord: Danda, double danda, digits ०-९ and the abbreviation sign are not word letters.
notes.replace: The normal form is NFC with every ZWJ and ZWNJ dropped (no "joiners" field), and the first two entries drop them before NFC as well. Mis-encoded independent vowels (अ + sign) are mended.
notes.phraseBreaks: The danda । and double danda ॥ end a sentence.
notes.signs: A vowel sign or virama must follow a consonant or nukta. Anusvara, candrabindu and visarga may follow a vowel (Bhojpuri हँ, में) and are not in this list.
notes.aksharantar: hin, Hindi's: Aksharantar and Dakshina have no Bhojpuri, and no other set of human Bhojpuri romanisations has an open licence. Bhojpuri is written in the same script and typed with the same habits, so the tables are fitted to Hindi's manual pairs. data/eval/bho/translit-human.tsv is therefore Hindi words, not a Bhojpuri test.
notes.translit: The pack's translit.mlkbnn is, for now, the Hindi pack's (packs/hi.neopack 2026.11.12, byte for byte): the same script, and a spelling model the Bhojpuri lexicon then filters. Its sources (Hindi Wikipedia and Wikisource, Dakshina, Aksharantar) are in the manifest's credits. A Bhojpuri one is trained by `make pack-models PACK_LANG=bho`: synthetic pairs of Bhojpuri's own words from this folder's tables, with Hindi's mined Aksharantar pairs beside them; when it replaces this one, take the three Hindi credits out and raise the version.
notes.minCount: 2, not the usual 3: the only openly licensed Bhojpuri text is its Wikipedia, far smaller than the other packs' text, and at 3 too many real words are lost.
